notes: All eight web searches ran (six required plus one on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors and one general AI search); none returned a statement by Van Orden about AI risk, superintelligence, a pause, or China talks. The official-site search found only his office's NDAA press releases (https://vanorden.house.gov/media/press-releases/van-orden-statement-fy2026-national-defense-authorization-act and https://vanorden.house.gov/media/press-releases/van-orden-applauds-committee-passage-fy26-national-defense-authorization-act), which list military AI provisions (joint AI research with partners such as Israel; a briefing on AI-enabled unmanned systems). These are bill summaries about military use of AI, not his own remarks on AI, and would be D under ruling 3; they were seen only in search-result excerpts and not opened. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced 24 September 2026 by Rep. Casar): search results describe the cosponsors as House Democrats; no source shows Van Orden as a cosponsor, though the full Congress.gov cosponsor list was not opened. No House letter on AI risk signed or led by him was found.
